screening.title: Incidence of lower limb tendinopathy: A 3-year prospective study of a youth elite athletes in a Brazilian sport club.
screening.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The purpose of this study was to investigate lower limb tendinopathy incidence over 3 seasons in Brazilian youth elite athletes., DESIGN: Prospective epidemiological study., METHODS: A prospective study was performed during 2015, 2016 and 2017 seasons, with a total of 1553 Brazilian youth athletes (1.195 male and 358 female) out of 6 sports (volleyball, basketball, judo, gymnastics, tennis and futsal). The mean age was 14.1 (11.2; 17.0) years, mean height was 1.75 (1.55; 1.95) meters and mean body mass was 59.4 (42.0; 76.4) kilograms. The diagnosis of lower limb tendinopathy (LLT) was made by an experienced sports physician based on a detailed history and clinical exam. The incidence of LLT was determined by number of injuries/total exposure hours x 1000., RESULTS: In total, 100 LLT were recorded during the 3 seasons. The most frequent type of LLT was patellar (79%), adductor (12%) and Achilles (9%). The frequency of patellar tendinopathy was higher in male's volleyball, basketball and female volleyball (41%, 25%, 13%, respectively) and the frequency of Achilles tendinopathy was higher in basketball and female volleyball (33%,22%). The LLT incidence was 2.5/1000h in 2015, 4.2/1000h in 2016 and 2.1/1000h in 2017., CONCLUSION: Lower limb tendinopathies are relatively common in youth elite athletes. In 3-season, the most frequent type was patellar tendinopathy. A higher LLT incidence was observed in male volleyball athletes when compared to female volleyball athletes. Basketball athletes presented a higher frequency of patellar, adductor and Achilles tendinopathies in 3-seasons when compared to other sports. Copyright © 2024. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

evidenceQuotes: The LLT incidence was 2.5/1000h in 2015, 4.2/1000h in 2016 and 2.1/1000h in 2017.

screening.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The purpose of this study was to investigate lower limb tendinopathy incidence over 3 seasons in Brazilian youth elite athletes., DESIGN: Prospective epidemiological study., METHODS: A prospective study was performed during 2015, 2016 and 2017 seasons, with a total of 1553 Brazilian youth athletes (1.195 male and 358 female) out of 6 sports (volleyball, basketball, judo, gymnastics, tennis and futsal). The mean age was 14.1 (11.2; 17.0) years, mean height was 1.75 (1.55; 1.95) meters and mean body mass was 59.4 (42.0; 76.4) kilograms. The diagnosis of lower limb tendinopathy (LLT) was made by an experienced sports physician based on a detailed history and clinical exam. The incidence of LLT was determined by number of injuries/total exposure hours x 1000., RESULTS: In total, 100 LLT were recorded during the 3 seasons. The most frequent type of LLT was patellar (79%), adductor (12%) and Achilles (9%). The frequency of patellar tendinopathy was higher in male's volleyball, basketball and female volleyball (41%, 25%, 13%, respectively) and the frequency of Achilles tendinopathy was higher in basketball and female volleyball (33%,22%). The LLT incidence was 2.5/1000h in 2015, 4.2/1000h in 2016 and 2.1/1000h in 2017., CONCLUSION: Lower limb tendinopathies are relatively common in youth elite athletes. In 3-season, the most frequent type was patellar tendinopathy. A higher LLT incidence was observed in male volleyball athletes when compared to female volleyball athletes. Basketball athletes presented a higher frequency of patellar, adductor and Achilles tendinopathies in 3-seasons when compared to other sports. Copyright © 2024. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

ai_raw_response.title: Incidence of lower limb tendinopathy: A 3-year prospective study of a youth elite athletes in a Brazilian sport club.
ai_raw_response.reason: Prospective club surveillance reports lower-limb tendinopathy outcomes for a separable elite youth futsal subgroup, with published incidence results per 1,000 exposure hours.
ai_raw_response.auditNotes: The paper reports sport-specific futsal incidence values, but its printed exposure total is cohort-wide rather than sport-specific. Inclusion relies on the paper's published incidence-rate table and its stated injuries-per-1,000-h definition; no exposure was calculated.
ai_raw_response.dataSource: Team-coach training and match-load questionnaires plus physician diagnosis in the club injury registry.
ai_raw_response.evidenceQuote: The LLT incidence was 2.5/1000h in 2015, 4.2/1000h in 2016 and 2.1/1000h in 2017.
evidenceQuotes: The LLT incidence was 2.5/1000h in 2015, 4.2/1000h in 2016 and 2.1/1000h in 2017.
Data collection involved volleyball, tennis, judo, gymnastic, futsal and basketball athletes.
Injury incidence expressed as number of injuries/1000 h of total exposure.
ai_raw_response.competitionContext: Traditional sport-club training and competitions over three seasons.
ai_raw_response.reportedDenominator: Published study rates: overall LLT incidence 2.5, 4.2 and 2.1 injuries per 1,000 h in 2015, 2016 and 2017; Table 1 separately lists futsal incidence values of 1.9, 4.4 and 0.6 under the table's injuries-per-1,000-h definition.
ai_raw_response.dataCollectionTiming: Sport exposure and injury data were collected across the 2015, 2016 and 2017 seasons.
ai_raw_response.populationEligibility: Brazilian youth elite futsal players within a multi-sport club (futsal n = 286 across the study cohort).
ai_raw_response.injuryIllnessDefinition: New musculoskeletal complaint from training or competition requiring medical assistance, recorded in a standardised injury registry.
ai_raw_response.denominatorEvidenceQuote: The LLT incidence was 2.5/1000h in 2015, 4.2/1000h in 2016 and 2.1/1000h in 2017.
